newsitem.title: UK: Water firms leak targets worth considering-UK MPs.
newsitem.headline: Water firms leak targets worth considering-UK MPs.

text.p: An all-party committee of the British parliament on Wednesday attacked water companies for a failure to set tough leakage reduction plans and said mandatory targets should be considered.
But the Environment Committee said the targets should be based on sophisticated criteria, not simply on the percentage of water running to waste in a company's area.
"We believe it is appropriate to consider setting mandatory leakage targets for the water companies," the committee said in a report.
Industry regulator OFWAT estimates that 30 percent of all water is lost to leakages, and the opposition Labour Party has already said it wants mandatory leakage targets.
The report said there was "room for reasonable doubt" about whether some water companies would meet their own declared long-term leakage targets.

It said only three -- United Utilities' (UU.L) North West Water, Severn Trent Plc and Southern Water Plc -- had set themselves tougher targets for 1997-8 than in their strategic business plans, while Thames Water and Yorkshire Water had set less demanding ones.
The report said it will be known in two years' time whether these 1997-8 targets have been achieved.
The committee recommended that by then, the regulator and the water companies should seek to agree "a methodology for setting mandatory targets which is not based on percentages."

It said this methodology should take into account operating pressures, whether distribution systems were urban or rural, the marginal cost of water, whether leaking water is reusable, and the condition of the distribution system.
The committee also recommended that water firms should be made responsible for the maintenance of customers' underground supply pipes.
It called on the government to commission a report into this idea looking at the possible costs and benefits and the legal implications.
